subtitle: When Talakadu Fell and Belur Rose

panels.shot: epic low-angle wide of Vishnuvardhana on war elephant overlooking the Kaveri at Talakadu, Belur temple silhouette ghosted behind
panels.action: Vishnuvardhana stands in armor atop a massive elephant on a sandy Kaveri riverbank, one hand raised toward a faint, radiant vision of the Chennakesava temple rising from mist behind him.

dialogue.text: In the year 1117, Bittideva—soon called Vishnuvardhana—broke Chola power at Talakadu and raised Belur’s Chennakesava, changing the faith and face of Karnataka without silencing its many voices.

i18n.hi: सन १११७ में बित्तिदेव — जो जल्द ही विष्णुवर्धन कहलाया — ने तलकाडु पर चोल सत्ता तोड़ी और बेलूर का चेन्नकेशव उठाया, कर्नाटक का रंग-रूप और धर्म बदलते हुए, उसके कई सुरों को जिंदा रखते हुए।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Vishnuvardhana seated in a forest court, half-light through foliage
panels.action: Young Vishnuvardhana sits on a simple but dignified throne of carved wood in a clearing, dense forest behind him, light streaking through leaves onto his thoughtful face.

dialogue.text: Before he was the lord of Belur, Bittideva ruled a forest kingdom in Gangavadi, a Hoysala chief among mightier powers, listening to the rustle of trees and the rumble of distant empires.

i18n.hi: बेलूर का स्वामी बनने से पहले, बित्तिदेव गंगवाडी के जंगल राज में राज करता था—हॉयसल सरदार, बड़े साम्राज्यों के बीच, पेड़ों की सरसराहट और दूर के साम्राज्यों की गड़गड़ाहट सुनता हुआ।

panels.shot: high-angle map-like wide showing Gangavadi between Chola lands and Western Ganga-Hoysala hills
panels.action: A stylized landscape shows hills and forested tracts of Gangavadi between a distant Chola-style cityscape to the east and rugged highlands to the west, with Vishnuvardhana standing at the center, hand on sword.

dialogue.text: To his east, the Cholas still claimed old Ganga lands along the Kaveri. To his west, the Hoysala strongholds watched. Gangavadi was both shield and prize.

i18n.hi: उसके पूरब में, चोल अभी भी कावेरी किनारे पुराने गंगा इलाकों का दावा करते थे। पश्चिम में हॉयसल किले नजर रखे थे। गंगवाडी ढाल भी था, इनाम भी।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a Jain-influenced court, with icons and scholars around
panels.action: Vishnuvardhana sits in court, flanked by dignitaries; on one side a Jain monk with calm bearing, on the other Brahmin advisors, behind them carved pillars with both Jina and Vishnu motifs.

dialogue.text: The Hoysalas’ early halls echoed with many voices—Jain teachers, temple priests, Kannada poets—each shaping a young king who would later choose a new path without erasing the old.

i18n.hi: हॉयसल दरबारों में शुरू से कई आवाजें थीं—जैन आचार्य, मंदिर के पुजारी, कन्नड कवि—सब मिलकर उस नौजवान राजा को गढ़ रहे थे जो बाद में नया रास्ता चुनेगा, बिना पुराना मिटाए।

panels.shot: dramatic medium shot of Vishnuvardhana receiving news from a messenger
panels.action: A dusty messenger kneels before Vishnuvardhana, breathless, as the king leans forward, fists clenched on his knees, the outlines of the Kaveri and sand dunes depicted on a cloth map between them.

dialogue.text: Around 1117, word reached his forest court: Chola authority still gripped Talakadu, the sand-bound gateway on the Kaveri. Whoever held it commanded the river and the road.

i18n.hi: लगभग १११७ में खबर उसके जंगल दरबार तक पहुंची: तलकाडु पर अब भी चोल हुकूमत है—कावेरी किनारे रेत में बसा दरवाजा। जो उसे थामे, वही नदी और सड़क पर हुक्म चलाए।

panels.shot: close-up on Vishnuvardhana’s face, resolve hardening
panels.action: Vishnuvardhana’s face fills the frame, eyes narrowed with resolve, the faint reflection of river water shimmering in his pupils.

dialogue.speaker: vishnuvardhana
dialogue.text: If the Kaveri is their strength, it must become ours.

i18n.hi: अगर कावेरी उनकी ताकत है, उसे हमारी भी बनाना होगा।

panels.shot: epic bird’s-eye over marching Hoysala forces through forest toward open sands
panels.action: Armored Hoysala cavalry and foot soldiers move in ordered columns through dense forest that opens toward pale sands and a glinting river, with Vishnuvardhana riding at the head.

dialogue.text: He rode south with his captains. Forest tracks led to open sand, and beyond the dunes lay Talakadu—Kaveri on one side, the Chola banner on the other.

i18n.hi: वो अपने सेनापतियों के संग दक्षिण को चला। जंगल पगडंडियां रेत के मैदान पर खुलीं, टीलों के पार तलकाडु था—एक तरफ कावेरी, दूसरी तरफ चोल ध्वज।

panels.shot: wide shot of Talakadu landscape, fort on dune, river flowing beside
panels.action: A fortified settlement stands partly buried in undulating sand, palm trees lining the nearby Kaveri, whose broad waters glint under the sun; Vishnuvardhana’s army appears on a ridge, tiny but determined.

dialogue.text: Talakadu was no simple town. Sand shifted around its walls, and the river was both moat and lifeline. For a century it had felt the weight of Chola feet.

i18n.hi: तलकाडु कोई साधारण कस्बा न था। रेत उसकी दीवारों के चारों ओर सरकती रहती, और नदी ही खाई भी थी, जीवन भी। एक सदी से चोल कदमों का भार वह झेल रहा था।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-wide of two armies facing off at a distance
panels.action: On the sands, two lines of soldiers face one another—Chola spearmen with tall standards, and Hoysala warriors with circular shields; Vishnuvardhana sits astride a horse in the foreground, watching the enemy.

dialogue.text: We do not have a poet’s detailed verse of that clash, only stone voices: Hoysalas took Talakadu from the Cholas. The sands became the stage of a turning tide.

i18n.hi: उस संग्राम का कोई कवि-वर्णन नहीं, बस पत्थर की आवाजें हैं: हॉयसल ने तलकाडु चोलों से छीना। रेत का मैदान बदलती लहरों की रंगभूमि बना।

panels.shot: tense medium shot as Vishnuvardhana signals advance
panels.action: Amid swirling dust, Vishnuvardhana raises his arm in a clear signal, his commanders leaning forward, troops beginning to surge across the sand toward the Chola line.

dialogue.text: When the dust settled, inscriptions remembered the outcome, not each stroke. The Hoysalas had broken Chola power on the Kaveri and stamped their own name on Gangavadi.

i18n.hi: जब धूल बैठ गई, शिलालेखों ने हर वार नहीं, बस नतीजा याद रखा। हॉयसल ने कावेरी पर चोल ताकत तोड़ी और गंगवाडी पर अपना नाम दर्ज कर दिया।

panels.shot: aftermath wide of captured Talakadu, Vishnuvardhana overlooking the town
panels.action: Vishnuvardhana stands on a dune above Talakadu’s now-quiet streets, the Chola banners taken down, Kaveri flowing steady behind him, as soldiers secure gates and speak with townsfolk.

dialogue.text: Holding Talakadu meant more than victory. It meant a river crossing, a trade artery, and a declaration whispered downstream: the Cholas could be pushed back.

i18n.hi: तलकाडु थामना सिर्फ जीत नहीं था। ये था नदी पार का फाटक, व्यापार की नस, और धारा के साथ फुसफुसाता ऐलान: चोलों को पीछे धकेला जा सकता है।

panels.shot: slow transition shot from battlefield to temple model in Vishnuvardhana’s hands
panels.action: The scene fades from the sandy battlefield to Vishnuvardhana now indoors, gazing at a small carved model of a temple in his hands, its base inscribed with faint decorative script.

dialogue.text: Soon, his mind turned from forts to stone. How should a forest kingdom announce its rising power and new devotion—not just on sand, but for centuries?

i18n.hi: जल्द ही उसका मन किलों से पत्थर की ओर मुड़ा। जंगल राज अपनी उभरती सत्ता और नई भक्ति कैसे दिखाए—सिर्फ रेत में नहीं, सदियों तक?

panels.shot: medium shot in Belur site, king among sculptors marking out temple lines
panels.action: On an open riverside ground at Belur, Vishnuvardhana stands with architects and sculptors as they stretch cords, mark the earth, and place the first foundation stones amid scattered blocks of soapstone.

dialogue.text: In Belur, on the Yagachi’s banks, he began what his inscription would call Vijaya-Narayana—Chennakesava, the beautiful Vishnu—founded in 1117 as both victory memorial and vow.

i18n.hi: यगाची किनारे बेलूर में उसने वो शुरू किया जिसे उसका शिलालेख विजय-नारायण कहेगा—चेन्नकेशव, रूपवान विष्णु—१११७ में उठाया गया विजय स्मारक भी, और एक प्रण भी।

panels.shot: close-up on sculptors’ hands carving intricate designs, Vishnuvardhana watching
panels.action: Skilled sculptors’ hands chip delicate patterns into dark stone—friezes of dancers, warriors, and gods—while Vishnuvardhana watches, arms folded, eyes following every curve.

dialogue.text: The Chennakesava temple grew as a statement in stone: of Vishnu’s grace, of Hoysala might, and of Kannada’s place beside Sanskrit in royal praise.

i18n.hi: चेन्नकेशव मंदिर पत्थर में बयान बनकर उठा: विष्णु की कृपा का, हॉयसल ताकत का, और राज स्तुति में संस्कृत के साथ कन्नड की जगह का।

panels.shot: medium shot in a court scene with Sri Vaishnava presence hinted, alongside Jain queen
panels.action: In the royal hall, Vishnuvardhana sits beside Queen Shantala, serene and dignified; nearby a Sri Vaishnava scholar in white and a Jain monk in simple robes converse quietly, showing different paths coexisting.

dialogue.text: Sri Vaishnava memory later sang of Ramanuja guiding him at Melkote. Inscriptions are silent on a single conversion moment, but loud on a king’s new Vishnu devotion among older Jain loyalties.

i18n.hi: श्रीवैष्णव यादें बाद में मेलकोटे में रामानुज के मार्गदर्शन की बात करती हैं। शिलालेख किसी एक परिवर्तन क्षण पर चुप हैं, पर पुराने जैन मानों के बीच राजा की नई विष्णु भक्ति पर जोर से बोलते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of Belur temple rising over years, workers of many backgrounds
panels.action: The temple’s main shrine stands largely complete, surrounded by scaffolding and busy artisans—sculptors, laborers, priests—suggesting long, multi-generational work as Vishnuvardhana walks through the site with ministers.

dialogue.text: Tradition speaks of a hundred years of work. The stones show many hands and decades, not a single moment—each carving adding another voice to a shared monument.

i18n.hi: परंपरा सौ बरस की मेहनत की बात करती है। पत्थर कई हाथों और कई दशकों की गवाही देता है, किसी एक पल की नहीं—हर नक्काशी साझा स्मारक में नई आवाज जोड़ती है।

panels.shot: intimate medium shot of Vishnuvardhana offering flowers before Chennakesava
panels.action: Within the cool, sculpted hall, Vishnuvardhana stands bareheaded before the Chennakesava image, offering a garland, lamps glowing softly around the idol’s tranquil face.

dialogue.text: When the consecration inscription was cut, it tied his name to Chennakesava and to Talakadu’s victory, binding politics, river sand and devotion into one record on stone.

i18n.hi: जब प्रतिष्ठा का शिलालेख काटा गया, उसने उसका नाम चेन्नकेशव और तलकाडु की जीत से जोड़ा—राजनीति, नदी की रेत और भक्ति, तीनों को एक पत्थर रिकॉर्ड में बांध दिया।

panels.shot: slow pull-back from temple to surrounding town with Jain and Vaishnava elements
panels.action: The camera pulls back from the temple tower to reveal Belur’s town around it: a Jain shrine, a Vaishnava matha, bustling markets, and villagers moving easily between them.

dialogue.text: Even after his Vaishnava turn, Jain generals like Ganggaraj built their own shrines. Belur’s streets held more than one kind of prayer under Chennakesava’s shadow.

i18n.hi: वैष्णव मार्ग अपनाने के बाद भी, गंगगराज जैसे जैन सेनानायक अपने मंदिर बनाते रहे। बेलूर की गलियों में चेन्नकेशव की छाया तले एक से ज्यादा तरह की प्रार्थनाएं गूंजती थीं।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide of Chennakesava temple at dawn, Vishnuvardhana’s figure faint in stone relief
panels.action: At dawn, the Chennakesava temple stands bathed in soft light, its walls crowded with carved figures; among them, a subtle relief of a royal patron hints at Vishnuvardhana’s enduring imprint.

dialogue.text: Talakadu’s sands still shift and Belur’s stones still shine, reminding us that real change, like Vishnuvardhana’s, is strongest when it carves space for many loyalties to stand together.

i18n.hi: तलकाडु की रेत आज भी सरकती है और बेलूर के पत्थर आज भी दमकते हैं, याद दिलाते हुए कि असली बदलाव, विष्णुवर्धन जैसा, तभी सबसे मजबूत होता है जब वो कई निष्ठाओं को साथ खड़े होने की जगह तराशता है।

subtitle_i18n.en: When Talakadu Fell and Belur Rose
